issues.description: Inconsistent response type and error handling for creating persons between the example Note endpoint and the implemented Person endpoint. The problem description and NoteResource use ResponseEntity to return HTTP status codes and bodies (e.g., POST /notes returns ResponseEntity<Note> and returns badRequest() when an ID is present). In the solution, createPerson is implemented to return a raw Person and returns null when input is invalid. This deviates from the pattern shown in NoteResource and from the explicit endpoint behavior described in the problem statement (which expects the saved person in the response body and implies proper HTTP codes). Students referring to NoteResource as guidance may be confused about whether to return ResponseEntity and how to signal bad requests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person create endpoint consistent with NoteResource and the problem description: change createPerson to return ResponseEntity<Person>, and on invalid input (e.g., person.getId() != null) return ResponseEntity.badRequest().build(); on success return ResponseEntity.ok(savedPerson). This keeps HTTP semantics clear and consistent for students following NoteResource as an example.
